Adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS). Both surface epithelium and endocervical glands are involved by AIS. At this power, nuclear hyperchromasia and crowding can be appreciated (A). full.description: This is a micrograph showing a histological section of the female reproductive system, specifically the cervix. The image displays the squamocolumnar junction, highlighting the transition between different types of epithelial cells. Cellular detail reveals nuclear characteristics and arrangement typical of this region under high magnification. The findings are consistent with normal histological architecture of the cervical transformation zone.

blind.description: This image is a micrograph of the cervix, specifically showing the squamocolumnar junction and endocervical glands. The sections display neoplastic columnar cells characterized by nuclear enlargement, hyperchromasia, pseudostratification, and numerous mitotic figures. There is an abrupt transition between the involved epithelium and normal tissue. The most likely diagnosis is adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS) of the cervix.

random.description: This is a photomicrograph of epithelial tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The image shows a cystic lumen lined by a continuous layer of stratified squamous epithelium. The lumen is extensively filled with orthokeratin material. These histological features are characteristic of an orthokeratinized odontogenic cyst or similar keratinous cyst.
